title: The Fall
timeline: Months 1-2, 298 AC. Winterfell and the wolfswood.
summary: Ser Torren Slate, a household knight of Blackpool seconded to Winterfell's guard, hears that the Hand of the King is dead and that Robert Baratheon is riding north. He scrubs a castle ready for a king, watches Lord Eddard Stark take a deserter's head, rides home through a summer snow where six pups are found, stands in the honour guard, drinks at a feast where a servant girl looks at him for exactly as long as it takes to walk past, and is crossing the yard on an ordinary morning when a boy falls off the Broken Tower. He is the first man to reach him.

scenes.title: Morning Duties
scenes.stage_directions: Opening scene. Mist on the training yard. Torren has been at a straw dummy since before light, which tells the player everything about him before he speaks. Ser Cley Stout watches from a fence rail eating an apple, which tells them everything about Cley. This is the movement and interact tutorial, and it carries the act's inciting news: Jon Arryn is dead and the king is riding north. CANON: Jon Arryn's death and Robert's journey to Winterfell to name Ned his Hand.

n1.speaker: cley
n1.text: You have been killing that straw man since before the sun was up. He is dead, Torren. He was dead when you started. At some point this stops being training and starts being a grudge.

n2.speaker: torren
n2.text: A knight keeps his sword arm sharp. You might try it.

n3.speaker: cley
n3.text: I keep my wits sharp. Far less sweat, and they work indoors.

n4.speaker: torren
n4.text: Your wits won't stop a blade.

n5.speaker: cley
n5.text: Nor will that straw man swing one. Leave off, now, and listen, because the whole castle is turned upside down this morning and you are the only man in it still hitting furniture. A raven came in the night.

choices.text: "From Lord Stark?"
"Out with it, then."

n6.speaker: cley
n6.text: From the south. Jon Arryn is dead. The Hand of the King.

n8.speaker: cley
n8.text: A fever, they say. Took him inside three days. But that is not the half of it, and the half of it is this: the king is riding north. Robert Baratheon himself, with the queen and half the court behind him, and they are coming here.

n10.speaker: cley
n10.text: Every man in this castle knows why, and every man is pretending he worked it out himself. He means to make Lord Stark his new Hand. There is nobody else he trusts.

choices.text: "...then there'll be a great many eyes on Winterfell, and some of them worth catching."
"...then the North loses its lord. That worries me."

n12.speaker: cley
n12.text: There it is. I can watch you doing the sum. Which of these strangers can be made to remember the name Slate.

n13.speaker: torren
n13.text: My house has served the Starks for three hundred years and got a draughty keep and a name nobody south of the Neck can pronounce. If there's a chance to be noticed I mean to take it.
n13.direction: The want, stated plainly in the first three minutes, so Act 5's ending has something to land on.

n14.speaker: cley
n14.text: You sound like my grandfather. The king comes to honour Lord Stark, not to sack the place.

n15.speaker: torren
n15.text: When great lords play at something, it's men like us who turn out to be the pieces.

n16.speaker: cley
n16.text: Very stirring. Ser Rodrik wants every man in the garrison in the yard within the hour. Lady Stark means to have this castle scrubbed to the mortar before Robert Baratheon sees a stone of it. Bring your arms and your worst temper.

scenes.title: Preparing for a King
scenes.stage_directions: First free-roam. Winterfell being scrubbed, hung with banners and emptied of anything embarrassing. Teaches the castle's geography before it is full of strangers, which is what makes the crowd of Act 1's later scenes legible. Four optional conversations. The player must report to Ser Rodrik and see to the stables to move on; the honour guard is optional and is the act's first piece of pure ambition.
objectives: Speak with Jory about the honour guard

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: Every banner in the North is being beaten, every hearth swept, every barrel of anything drinkable counted twice. Winterfell has not been this frightened of a guest in living memory.

n10.speaker: rodrik_cassel
n10.text: Good, another pair of hands. Lady Stark wants the yard cleared and the guest chambers aired. A hundred knights, twice as many servants, and every one of them expecting a bed. We have not housed so many since Lord Stark's wedding, and I was younger then and it nearly killed me.

choices.text: "Where do you want me, ser?"
"A hundred knights. This place will burst."

n11.speaker: rodrik_cassel
n11.text: Aye, and half of them Lannisters. The queen travels with both her brothers. Ser Jaime of the Kingsguard, and the small one. Lord Stark is not pleased and has not said so, which is how you know.

n12.speaker: rodrik_cassel
n12.text: The stables. We need room for the royal horses, and those animals are better bred than most of the men on them. After that find Jory. He is making up an honour guard to ride out and meet the column on the road.

n13.speaker: rodrik_cassel
n13.text: They came late to Robert's war and the North remembers. But a queen is a queen. Keep your opinions off your face when you see that white cloak, ser. Lord Stark would expect no less, and I expect it louder.

n20.speaker: jory_cassel
n20.text: Come about the honour guard. You are the fourth today. I can use riders, but understand what this is: we are Winterfell's face on that road. Can you sit a horse without falling off it?

choices.text: "I was born in a saddle, and you know it."
"Better than Theon Greyjoy, at any rate."
"I'd rather have the work than the honour, ser."

n21.speaker: jory_cassel
n21.text: You were born in Blackpool like the rest of us and there is one horse in it. You are in. Dawn, three days. House colours and a cloak that has not been slept in.

n22.speaker: jory_cassel
n22.text: Ha. The Greyjoy boy rides well enough when he is not admiring himself in his own greaves. You are in. Dawn, three days. Do not be late, ser, I will not wait for you and I will enjoy not waiting.

n23.speaker: jory_cassel
n23.text: That is the right answer and it is also a way of not asking for what you want. I will put you down anyway. Dawn, three days.

n24.speaker: jory_cassel
n24.text: And polish everything. The king is a drunk and a glutton and he can still pick the one soldier out of a line of forty. He has been doing it since before you were born.

n30.speaker: stable_hand
n30.text: The king! The actual king, here, in this yard. Do you think he wears the crown all the time? Even asleep?

choices.text: "I doubt it. They say he's grown too fat for ceremony."
"Kings are men who sit in taller chairs. Don't work yourself up."

n31.speaker: stable_hand
n31.text: Fat? Robert Baratheon? The man who put a hammer through Rhaegar Targaryen on the Trident? That cannot be right.
n31.direction: The only time the word Targaryen appears in Chapter 1, and it is about a dead man on a battlefield, spoken by a stable boy who has never left the winter town. It is a war story, not a hint, and nothing in the act connects it to the girl.

n32.speaker: stable_hand
n32.text: Easy for you to say, ser. You have been places. I have never been past the winter town in my life.

n42.speaker: hodor
n42.direction: He is carrying a barrel that would take three other men. Nobody in the scene remarks on it.

n50.speaker: narrator
n50.text: The stables, swept down to the flags and re-strawed twice. There is room for forty more horses than Winterfell has ever needed, and in three days there will not be enough.

scenes.title: A Deserter's Head
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: the execution of Gared, deserter of the Night's Watch, by Eddard Stark, witnessed by Bran at seven. Twenty riders in a ragged half-circle around a stump in old snow. This is the movement and interact tutorial: the player is free to walk the ring and speak to four men before the axe. The camera never frames the block. It frames Bran. Composer: no music under the execution itself, only wind and the sound of twenty horses breathing.
objectives: Take your place in the ring
Speak with the men of the household

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: Summer snow, three inches of it, and every man in the party pretending he is not cold.
n1.direction: Fires on level load. Italic, centred, fades.

n2.speaker: hune
n2.text: Slate. You'll stand at the left of the ring and you'll keep your mouth shut through it. Lord Stark does this himself and he does it quiet.

choices.text: "Has he done many?"
Say nothing and take your place.

n4.speaker: hune
n4.text: Enough that he's stopped counting and not so many he's stopped minding. That's the whole of it. Don't ask him.

n5.speaker: torren
n5.text: I wasn't going to ask him.

n6.speaker: narrator
n6.text: The ring closes. The deserter is brought out. He does not struggle, and somehow that is worse.

n12.speaker: jory_cassel
n12.text: Then here's the only advice worth having. Watch the boy, not the block. Lord Stark brought him out here to learn something and I'd wager you learn it faster.

choices.text: "Learn what?"
"I know what."

n14.speaker: jory_cassel
n14.text: That the man who passes the sentence swings the sword. It's a Stark thing. It sounds like a saying until you've watched him do it, and then it isn't one.

n15.speaker: jory_cassel
n15.text: Do you. Well. Watch anyway, ser, and tell me after whether you knew it or only heard it.

n20.speaker: theon_greyjoy
n20.text: Blackpool, isn't it. Slate. I keep meaning to ask what your house does.

n22.speaker: theon_greyjoy
n22.text: Yes. That's what I thought it did.

choices.text: "And what does yours hold, my lord?"
Let it go.

n23.speaker: theon_greyjoy
n23.text: Ha. Nothing at all, ser. Nothing at all. I like you better than I expected to and I expect that to pass.

n24.speaker: narrator
n24.text: He smiles at you for a moment longer than he needs to, and turns his horse away.

n30.speaker: robb_stark
n30.text: You're one of Lord Ondrew's. Torren.

n32.speaker: robb_stark
n32.text: My father makes me learn them. All of them. Every man who owes us service and every man he owes it back to. He says a lord who can't name his own household has already lost it.

n33.speaker: torren
n33.text: That's a great many names, my lord.

n34.speaker: robb_stark
n34.text: It is. Ask me again in ten years and I'll have forgotten half.
n34.direction: He will not. Act 3 pays this off: Robb names every lord in the yard without looking at a list.

n40.speaker: cley
n40.text: Fourth deserter this year. That is what Jory says. Fourth.

n41.speaker: torren
n41.text: Look at his face, Cley. He isn't running from the Wall. He's running from something and the Wall was in the way.

choices.text: "What's worse than the Wall?"
Keep it to yourself.

n42.speaker: cley
n42.text: Nothing. That is the whole point of the Wall. It is the worst thing there is, which is why they put it at the end.
n42.direction: Both of them are wrong and the game never tells them so. The prologue is not dramatised and this is the only place its shadow reaches Act 1.

n43.speaker: narrator
n43.text: You keep it to yourself. The man dies without anybody having asked him a single question, which is the part you think about afterwards.

scenes.title: Six Pups and a Seventh
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: the direwolf bitch dead in the snow with a broken antler in her throat; five pups; the albino found apart, silent, eyes open. Free-roam along a stretch of road. The dead direwolf is a fixed point the player will find; the albino is off the path and only found if the player wanders, which is the point. Composer: the road theme drops out entirely at the carcass and does not come back until the party remounts.

n1.speaker: hune
n1.text: Column's stopped. Go and see why, and if it's a fallen horse don't come back and tell me it's an omen.

n2.speaker: narrator
n2.text: It is not a fallen horse.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: A direwolf, dead in the snow, larger than any wolf has a right to be. A shard of antler in her throat. Five pups blind against her cold flank, still trying.

n11.speaker: theon_greyjoy
n11.text: Mercy would be quicker. I'll do it if nobody else has the stomach.

n13.speaker: narrator
n13.text: Bran is holding one already. Nobody saw him pick it up.

choices.text: "There's a sigil dead in the road, my lord. That's all anyone will say of it."
"Five pups, five Stark children. Six, with the bastard."
Say nothing. It is not your family.

n14.speaker: robb_stark
n14.text: Men will say what they like. I'd rather they said we found them than we left them.

n15.speaker: narrator
n15.text: Jon Snow does not look at you. Lord Stark does, once, and then agrees to it, and you spend some time afterwards wondering which of those two things you did.

n16.speaker: narrator
n16.text: You hold your horse and your tongue, and the decision is made without you, as most are.

n20.speaker: narrator
n20.text: Off the road, twenty paces into the trees, a sixth pup. White as the snow it is sitting in. It is not crying. Its eyes are already open, and they are red, and they are on you.
n20.direction: Optional discovery. Ghost. The player finds this only by leaving the road. No dialogue follows; Jon collects him a beat later.

scenes.title: The King Comes North
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: the royal party arrives at Winterfell; the household kneels; Robert goes straight to the crypts. Torren is pinned in the honour guard and cannot move more than two tiles. The player can look, and looking is the whole scene: the wheelhouse, the gold cloaks, the Kingsguard white, the queen who does not get down, and somewhere in the baggage train at the back, a girl with a covered head carrying water. She is on screen. The player is not meant to notice her. NYRA IS ON SCREEN HERE AND IS NOT FLAGGED. This is deliberate.

n1.speaker: hune
n1.text: Straight back. Eyes front. If your knee's not down before the king's boot touches the stone I'll have it off you.

n2.speaker: narrator
n2.text: Four hundred riders. You have never seen four hundred of anything.

n3.speaker: wells
n3.text: Northern knight, are you? I'd not have guessed it from the mail. Who dubbed you, ser? Anyone I'd know?

choices.text: "A hedge knight. In a field, in the rain."
"Lord Slate of Blackpool saw it done."
Keep your eyes front.

n4.speaker: wells
n4.text: In the rain. Gods, that's honest. I'd have lied. Well, ser, we'll see what it's worth when there's something to be brave at.
n4.direction: Wells respects the honesty and will say so again in Act 5, over Torren's shoulder, at the Camps.

n5.speaker: wells
n5.text: Saw it done. Saw. There's a word doing a great deal of work.

n6.speaker: narrator
n6.text: He waits. He is good at waiting. Eventually he laughs at something else.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: The king is enormous and he is not what the songs said. He takes Lord Stark by the shoulders in front of everyone, and then he says something quiet, and they go down into the ground together.

n20.speaker: cley
n20.text: That is the man who killed Rhaegar Targaryen on the Trident. That one. Getting off that horse.

n21.speaker: torren
n21.text: Hold your tongue. He is still the king.

n22.speaker: cley
n22.text: I know it. I am not laughing, Torren. I had a picture of him in my head since I was six years old and I have just had it taken off me in a courtyard, and I find I mind.
n22.direction: Cley's one unguarded moment in the act. He does not get another until the walls in s1_12.

scenes.title: Torchlight
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: Robert descends to Lyanna's tomb and speaks with Ned about her. EDGE proximity: Torren holds a torch at the stair-head, twelve paces back, and hears fragments. The player cannot descend. The player CAN choose to move one tile closer, twice, and each step earns a clearer fragment and a small risk. Composer: no score. Dripping, and two men's voices in stone.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: They took a torch and left you holding another, which is a way of saying stay here without troubling to say it.

n2.speaker: narrator
n2.text: Sound carries badly in the crypts, and then all at once very well.

choices.text: Step closer.
Stay where you were put.

n3.speaker: robert_baratheon
n3.text: ...seventeen years and they still put her down here in the dark. She should have a hill and the wind on it.

choices.text: Step closer again.
That is enough.

n4.speaker: eddard_stark
n4.text: She's home. That was the whole of what she asked me for.

n5.speaker: robert_baratheon
n5.text: She asked you. She never asked me for anything, Ned, not once, not in her whole life.

n6.speaker: narrator
n6.text: A long silence with two men in it. Then the sound of a big man breathing badly, and you go back up the stair very quietly, and you take the sound with you, and you never repeat it to anyone.

n8.speaker: narrator
n8.text: You hold the torch until your arm shakes, and you hear only the shape of it, and not one word.

scenes.title: The Welcoming Feast
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: the welcoming feast at Winterfell. Free-roam of a hot, loud, crowded hall. Six optional conversations. Torren is on the lowest bench, which is correct and which he minds. BRIEF ENCOUNTER #1 fires here: a servant girl on a fixed patrol route crosses the hall with a wine jug. If the player's facing intersects her path within two tiles, hold one frame of eye contact, no music sting, no camera push, and set act1_encounter_feast. If the player follows her, she looks back once at the door. She has no dialogue. She never speaks in Act 1. Her sprite is silver-haired under a plain grey coif that does not quite cover it.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: Winterfell has not been this loud in living memory and will not be again.

n10.speaker: hune
n10.text: Look at it. Half the realm in one hall and every one of them certain they're the important half.

n12.speaker: hune
n12.text: We're the half that's still standing at the end, lad, because we didn't drink the good stuff.

n20.speaker: jory_cassel
n20.text: You've been staring at the high table for a quarter hour.

n22.speaker: jory_cassel
n22.text: Aye. Everybody at this end counts it. Here's the trick of it, ser. Nobody up there is counting back.

choices.text: "Then I'll give them something to count."
"That's a hard thing to hear."
"I'm content where I sit."

n23.speaker: jory_cassel
n23.text: That's what they all say at your age and I've buried a fair number of them. Do it anyway. Just don't do it in a hurry.

n24.speaker: jory_cassel
n24.text: It's a true one. There's worse to hear and you'll hear that too.

n25.speaker: jory_cassel
n25.text: No you're not. Drink your ale, ser.

n30.speaker: wells
n30.text: In the rain, he says! In a field! Sers, I give you the knighthood of the North.

choices.text: Laugh with them.
"It was raining. You'd have drowned in it, ser."
Stand up and leave the table.

n31.speaker: narrator
n31.text: You laugh. It comes out a half-beat late and everyone at the table hears the half-beat.

n32.speaker: wells
n32.text: Ha! There he is. Sit down, Blackpool, you've earned the jug.

n33.speaker: narrator
n33.text: You leave with your cup, and behind you the table finds something else to be funny about within a count of ten, which is the part that stings.

n40.speaker: narrator
n40.text: A servant girl crossing with a jug. Grey coif, silver hair escaping it, eyes you would call dark until the torch swings and they are not dark at all.
n40.direction: BRIEF ENCOUNTER #1. Fires on facing-intersect only. No portrait, no name plate, no music cue. One node, then she is past. She does not speak.

n41.speaker: narrator
n41.text: She looks at you for as long as it takes to walk four paces. Then the hall closes behind her.

n42.speaker: narrator
n42.text: At the door she looks back. Not at the hall. Then she is gone into the kitchens and the noise comes back in.
n42.direction: Only fires if the player followed her. Optional flavour, no mechanical effect beyond the flag.

n44.speaker: torren
n44.direction: CHAPTER 1 RULE: neither Targaryen nor Valyrian is spoken here, and Torren does not reach for either. He gets two words out and Cley steps on the third, and the player supplies whatever they like.

choices.text: "...never mind. Pass the jug."
"They were the wrong colour for a serving girl."

n45.speaker: cley
n45.text: That is the spirit. To the king, and more particularly to the king's cellar.

n46.speaker: cley
n46.text: The wrong colour. Torren, half this hall is the queen's household and the other half came up the kingsroad from places you and I have never been. There are a hundred kinds of face down here that were not made in the North. Drink your ale.
n46.direction: Wrong theory number one, delivered with total confidence and never corrected. Baelish gives number two in Act 2; Cersei implies number three in Act 4.

n50.speaker: narrator
n50.text: Benjen Stark is down the hall in Night's Watch black, talking to his nephew, who is sitting apart from his family at a lower table with a wolf pup under his feet and a face like a closed door.

n51.speaker: narrator
n51.text: At the far end, the queen's younger brother is drinking with a jug in either hand and laughing louder than men twice his height, and doing it deliberately, and watching the room over the rim the entire time.

scenes.title: Days of Feasting
scenes.stage_directions: Second free-roam, and the act's breathing room. The royal party has settled in and several days pass. Robert hunts. Cersei keeps to her chambers. Lannister and Stark men circle each other in the yard without ever quite starting anything. Four optional conversations, each of which the player will remember for a different reason later: Robb (who Torren follows to war), Jon (who leaves and never comes back into the frame), Tyrion (a Lannister who is decent to him, which complicates Act 5), Benjen (who says a true thing about the Wall that nobody in this game has time for). Composer: the warm Winterfell theme, and it is the last time it is heard warm.

n1.speaker: cley
n1.text: Nine days they have been here. Nine. The king has hunted four times, drunk through the cellar, and has not once been seen before noon. I have never admired a man so much.

n10.speaker: robb_stark
n10.text: You fight well. I have been watching. Ser Rodrik says you have a clean arm and a bad temper about it.

choices.text: "Ser Rodrik is generous. I've a great deal still to learn."
"I'd welcome a match, my lord, if you're willing."

n11.speaker: robb_stark
n11.text: Then we should train together. Jon and I spar every morning, but Jon is going to the Wall with my uncle. I am about to be very short of anyone who will hit me properly.

n12.speaker: robb_stark
n12.text: Willing. Gods, yes. Everyone in this yard holds back because my father is lord and they think I cannot tell. Jon never does, and Jon is the best of us for it. Take a practice sword.

n13.speaker: narrator
n13.text: He is fourteen and he is quick and he is nowhere near as good as he believes. He also does not stop, not once, not even when he should, and that is the thing you find you cannot teach out of him and would not want to.
n13.direction: The player fights Robb in a no-stakes practice bout. He cannot be beaten badly and cannot win. Both actors end on one hp of a practice bar.

n20.speaker: jon_snow
n20.text: You are one of the mountain houses. North of the wolfswood.

choices.text: "Blackpool. A small house and an old one."
"You know your maps. Most southrons couldn't find us on one."

n21.speaker: jon_snow
n21.text: Small houses are honest houses. Nobody in them is pretending to be something else. I am going to the Wall. My uncle says they need men.

n22.speaker: jon_snow
n22.text: I have read every map in Maester Luwin's library twice. When you cannot leave a place you learn the whole world outside it instead.

choices.text: "You'd give up lands, a wife, sons? All of it?"
Let it be. He has clearly decided.

n24.speaker: jon_snow
n24.text: Give up what? I am a bastard. I will never inherit, never sit in my father's seat, never carry the name. The Wall is the only place in the world where none of that signifies. It is not a sacrifice, ser. It is the first good offer anyone has made me.

n25.speaker: narrator
n25.text: He nods at you and goes back to the dummies, and hits one considerably harder than the drill calls for, and you leave him to it.

n30.speaker: tyrion_lannister
n30.text: A Northern knight. Delightful. Tell me, is it true that up here men judge one another by how long they can stand in snow without mentioning it?

choices.text: "Only Starks do that, my lord. The rest of us light a fire."
"You'd be Tyrion Lannister. The Imp."

n31.speaker: tyrion_lannister
n31.text: Ha! A Northerner with a sense of humour. I should have you stuffed and mounted. Drink with me, ser — I find wine improves all company, and mine most of all.

n32.speaker: tyrion_lannister
n32.text: The very one. Though I answer to Tyrion. The Imp is what men call me when they believe I cannot hear them, and I can always hear them. It is nearly as useful as being underestimated, which is the other thing I have instead of a sword.

n33.speaker: narrator
n33.text: He is the only Lannister in this castle who has spoken to you as though you were in the room. You will remember that in a wood in the Riverlands, some months from now, with his family's men in front of you.
n33.direction: Seeds the complication for Act 5. Not paid off in Chapter 1.

n40.speaker: benjen_stark
n40.text: You have the look of a man who keeps his oaths. The Watch could use those. Have you ever thought of taking the black?

choices.text: "My sword's sworn to Winterfell. But I honour those that guard the Wall."
"I mean to make a name for my house first."

n41.speaker: benjen_stark
n41.text: Winterfell needs good men too. But hear me, ser, since nobody else in this castle will: the Watch is weaker every year. Six hundred men on a wall built for ten thousand. A day is coming when the North will have to remember there is a Wall and why anyone bothered.
n41.direction: The truest thing said by anyone in Act 1, delivered to a man who has no way to act on it, in a game that never goes to the Wall. Left entirely unresolved.

n42.speaker: benjen_stark
n42.text: A name. Aye. I wanted one of those, before I took the black. Hold it carefully — a name is a great deal easier to lose than it is to earn.

n50.speaker: narrator
n50.text: On the ninth day the king announces he will hunt again, and half the castle rides out with him at first light, and Winterfell is quieter than it has been in a fortnight.

scenes.title: The Broken Tower
scenes.stage_directions: ACT CLIMAX. CANON: Bran climbs the Broken Tower, sees Jaime and Cersei, and is pushed. Staged as an ordinary errand across an ordinary yard. Torren is carrying a bundle of lances. The player can look up and see a small figure on the wall - this is optional and most players will. There is no way to intervene. Nobody is meant to feel they could have. The sound happens off-camera and the camera does NOT whip to it; Torren turns at a walking pace, because that is what a man actually does. Composer: birds and a hammer in the forge, then nothing at all. DECIDED: Torren does NOT see anyone at the window. He sees a shuttered window in a tower nobody enters, and that is the whole of his evidence, forever. He never connects it and no character in the North ever learns Bran was pushed. The player, who watched it from the yard, carries that alone into Act 3.
objectives: Carry the lances to the yard

n1.speaker: hune
n1.text: Lances to the yard, and then you can sleep off whatever you did to yourself last night.

n2.speaker: narrator
n2.text: The castle is half empty. Half the household is still abed and the other half is being quiet about it.

n10.speaker: narrator
n10.text: High up on the Broken Tower, something moves. A boy, hand over hand, going up the outside of a ruin as easily as most men use a stair.
n10.direction: Optional look-up trigger. If the player does not look, the flag is not set and n11 does not play.

n11.speaker: torren
n11.text: Gods. He does that every day, they say.

n12.speaker: narrator
n12.text: A window in the Broken Tower is shuttered from the inside. There is nobody in that tower. There has not been anybody in that tower in a hundred years.
n12.direction: Optional. AFTER-grade proximity on the Jaime/Cersei beat. The player is given the fact and no interpretation.

n20.speaker: narrator
n20.text: The sound is not loud. That is the thing nobody tells you about it. It is a small sound and then the yard is entirely silent.
n20.direction: THE FALL. Camera does not move. Torren turns over four frames. Player regains control and can walk - not run. Running is disabled for this beat.

n21.speaker: narrator
n21.text: You reach him first. You are the first man there and you will think about that for the rest of your life, because there is nothing at all that being first gets you.

n22.speaker: torren
n22.text: He's breathing. Somebody get the maester. SOMEBODY GET THE MAESTER.

n23.speaker: narrator
n23.text: A direwolf pup is already there, standing over the boy, and it will not let the second man near.

n24.speaker: catelyn_stark
n24.text: Don't move him. Don't - carry him. Carry him. Carefully. Ser. Carefully.

n25.speaker: narrator
n25.text: He weighs nothing. That is the other thing nobody tells you.
n25.direction: The player walks Bran to the maester's turret. No choices, no interaction, no music. Roughly ninety seconds of walking. This is the act's last playable beat and it must feel too long.

scenes.title: Aftermath
scenes.stage_directions: Hours after the fall. The hunting party comes back at speed, having been recalled. Ned is off his horse before it stops. Robb runs. The direwolf pup has not stopped howling and does not stop for the whole scene, at a volume that is slightly too loud for comfort in the mix. The player is free to walk a castle that has become a sickroom, and will end up in the godswood whether they meant to or not. Composer: nothing but the wolf.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: The hunting party comes back through the gate at a gallop with the horns still going, because nobody thought to stop blowing them. Lord Stark is off his horse before it halts and across the yard without a word to anyone.

n2.speaker: narrator
n2.text: Robb goes past you at a dead run with his face the colour of the walls. Jon Snow follows him. The king comes last, and is bellowing for wine before his feet are on the stones, and it is not entirely clear that he has understood what he was recalled for.

n3.speaker: cley
n3.text: Maester Luwin has not left him. Lady Stark has not eaten and will not leave the room. They say he may not wake at all.

n4.speaker: torren
n4.text: He climbed that tower every day of his life, Cley. Every day since he could walk. He never fell once.

choices.text: "Not once. And then today."
Say nothing more about it.

n5.speaker: cley
n5.text: There is always a first time. That is what a first time is.
n5.direction: Cley is not being callous. He is closing a door that Torren should not be standing in, and he knows it, and he does it anyway because they are both household men in a castle full of the king's people.

n6.speaker: narrator
n6.text: You do not say it and Cley does not ask, and the two of you stand in the yard for a while not saying it, which is its own kind of conversation.

n7.speaker: narrator
n7.text: The wolf has not stopped. It has been going since the morning, from the window of the room they carried him to, and every man in this castle has stopped hearing it and none of them have stopped hearing it.

n20.speaker: narrator
n20.text: You find yourself in the godswood without any clear memory of walking there. The heart tree's face is carved deep and the sap in the cuts has gone dark and the black pool underneath it does not move at all.

n21.speaker: narrator
n21.text: Your house keeps the old gods, which in Blackpool means a stand of three alders and a great deal of forgetting. You have never been much good at this and you are not sure why you came.

choices.text: Pray for the boy.
Think about the shutter.
Stand there. Say nothing.

n22.speaker: torren
n22.text: I don't know how this is meant to go. He's seven. That's all I've got.

n23.speaker: torren
n23.text: There was a shutter closed in a tower nobody goes into. That's all it was. A closed shutter.
n23.direction: He gets no further than this and never will. He has one fact, it is not enough, and it stays not enough for the rest of the chapter. The player has been shown considerably more than he has.

n24.speaker: narrator
n24.text: You stand in front of it until your feet go cold. Whatever is supposed to happen does not, and you find you are not surprised and not especially disappointed either.

n25.speaker: narrator
n25.text: The red eyes look at nothing in particular. Behind you, a long way off, the wolf is still going.

scenes.title: The Road South
scenes.stage_directions: CANON: the royal party departs Winterfell for King's Landing with Ned, Sansa and Arya; Jon rides north with Tyrion and Benjen. BRIEF ENCOUNTER #2, scripted, unmissable. A servant girl loses her grip on a trunk in the press of the yard; Torren catches it. Four frames of overlapping hands. Neither speaks. If the player mashes interact, Torren says something, and it is the wrong thing, and it is recorded. Act card follows.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: They go south at dawn with the boy still asleep in the turret behind them, and nobody says the obvious thing about that.

n2.speaker: narrator
n2.text: The yard is all elbows. A trunk goes out of a girl's hands at the level of your chest and you have it before you have decided to.

n3.speaker: narrator
n3.text: Her hands are still on it. Yours are under it. Four frames, and the yard shoves past on both sides.
n3.direction: Hold. Genuinely hold. No music change. She does not speak and the player is given the option to, which is a trap.

choices.text: Say nothing. Set it on the cart.
"Careful."

n4.speaker: narrator
n4.text: It comes out flat, and it sounds like a rebuke, and it is not one, and there is no time at all to fix it. She takes the trunk. She is already three people away.

n5.speaker: narrator
n5.text: You do not learn her name. She does not learn yours. Two hours later the column is a smudge on the kingsroad and Winterfell is very, very quiet.

n6.speaker: hune
n6.text: Well. That's that, then. Back to it, ser.

scenes.title: Winter Is Coming
scenes.stage_directions: ACT CLOSE. Torren on the rampart watching the column shrink on the kingsroad. Below in the yard, Robb Stark alone with his direwolf, suddenly the eldest man in his family present. From the turret window, the wolf. The camera pulls back slowly off the wall until Winterfell is small and the North is not. Act card, then Act 2 and a POV change the player has not been warned about.

n1.speaker: narrator
n1.text: The column goes over the southern hills a piece at a time and then all at once. The kingsroad is empty and grey and looks like it has never had anybody on it.

n2.speaker: narrator
n2.text: Below in the yard, Robb Stark is standing on his own with his wolf. His father is gone south, his uncle north, his brother to the Wall, his sisters with the king, his mother upstairs with a boy who will not wake. He is fourteen and he is the eldest Stark in Winterfell and he is standing very straight about it.

n3.speaker: cley
n3.text: Well. You wanted eyes on this place. You have got them. The whole realm knows where Winterfell is now.

choices.text: "That isn't what I meant and you know it."
"Aye. I did want that."

n4.speaker: cley
n4.text: No. But it is what you asked for, and I have noticed the gods are very literal.

n5.speaker: cley
n5.text: I know. That is why I said it. You are not a bad man, Torren, you are only a hungry one, and this castle is about to find out what that is worth.

n6.speaker: narrator
n6.text: From the turret window the wolf is still going. Maester Luwin says the boy lives. He does not say he will wake, and he is careful about it in the way maesters are careful when they have already decided.

n7.speaker: narrator
n7.text: You look north instead, because it is easier, and the sky over the wolfswood is darker than it has any business being at this hour of a summer morning.

n8.speaker: narrator
n8.text: The Starks have been saying the same three words for eight thousand years and everyone in the North repeats them without hearing them, the way you say a thing about weather.
n8.direction: The words themselves are never spoken by a character in this game. The act is named for them and they are left in the player's mouth.
